item.title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
item.description: arXiv:2610.18949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure $ABX_3$ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6$\times$ on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

item.title: Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
item.description: arXiv:2610.18999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.

item.title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
item.description: arXiv:2610.19112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transparent conductors are key functional materials in modern optoelectronic devices. Their performance is governed by an inherent trade-off between optical transparency and electrical conductivity. Correlated metallic oxides offer an attractive workaround to this compromise, where narrow partially-filled bands provide high conductivity, while the absence of visible-range transitions enables optical transparency. Despite this promise, transparency and conductivity remain coupled through carrier density and electronic coherence. Here, we use proximity to a metal-insulator transition (MIT) as a design principle for engineering this balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors. Epitaxial Ti-substituted $SrVO_3$ films serve as a model platform where the optical window and metallicity are tuned simultaneously. We demonstrate and explain a systematic broadening of the optical window to regimes relevant for silicon photovoltaics. This gain is counterbalanced by carrier depletion and disorder, which drive the loss of coherent transport near the composition-driven MIT. A Haacke figure-of-merit analysis identifies the optimal composition range near the MIT, where the loss of metallic transport is accompanied by persistent near-Fermi-level spectral weight, indicating disorder-assisted localization together with correlation-driven spectral-weight redistribution. These findings establish proximity to an MIT as a general materials-design strategy, using electronic filling as a tuning knob for the transparency-conductivity balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors.

item.title: Symmetry-selected extreme shear compliance in a stable carbon monolayer
item.description: arXiv:2610.19168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solids that are stiff to most loads and extremely compliant to one are normally built, not found. That internal atomic relaxation lowers elastic constants is textbook; what has remained untested is whether it can be driven far enough to separate the elastic scales of a crystal by an order of magnitude while leaving it mechanically stable. Density functional theory calculations of the complete in-plane elastic tensor of four non-hexagonal carbon monolayers sharing a square lattice metric show that it can: their longitudinal stiffnesses agree to within a factor of two while their shear constants span more than a factor of fifty. Twin T-graphene, previously reported as elastically isotropic from normal strains alone, is the extreme case, with $C_{66}=3.03$~N\,m$^{-1}$, nearly fifty times below graphene, at an axial stiffness typical of semiconducting monolayers, and a soft Kelvin eigenvalue a factor of $29$ below the others while the Born criteria hold. Symmetry confines the strain-induced relaxation to the $B_{2g}$ sector, a counter-torsion of the carbon sublayers about the short mid-plane bonds that removes $96\%$ of the clamped-ion shear stiffness with almost no bond stretching and leaves the semiconducting gap intact. Transverse acoustic phonons, finite-temperature dynamics, and large-deformation simulations show that the channel survives beyond the harmonic, zero-temperature limit. Because the selection rule is a point-group statement rather than a chemical one, it yields a screening criterion for other crystals and other strain components.

item.title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.

item.title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.19404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reticular chemistry allows metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be designed from their building units, yet their synthesis remains constrained by sparse experimental data, noisy crystallization outcomes, and the absence of benchmarks for comparing active-learning strategies. While data-driven approaches such as Bayesian optimization (BO) can improve synthesis success rates, selecting appropriate optimizers beforehand for mapping MOF crystallization landscapes remains largely empirical. Here we present ActMOF, an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing search strategies in aluminum-carboxylate MOF synthesis. ActMOF is emulated from experimentally measured microwave syntheses with each encoded condition assigned a crystallinity index calculated based on diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum. By benchmarking policies guided by Gaussian processes (GP), tree ensembles and large language models (LLM), ActMOF placed the GP family among the leading policies for active learning in sparse synthesis landscapes. It then demonstrated transferability by guiding the microwave synthesis of six reticularly related aluminum MOFs. All six campaigns gave crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each, and established a reusable testbed for AI-driven MOF synthesis.

item.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moir\'e-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moir\'e superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.19542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semiconductor moir\'e superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moir\'e potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moir\'e intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moir\'e-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. Moreover, we demonstrate efficient pressure control over the interplay between charges and both intralayer and interlayer excitons: the intralayer charge-transfer exciton becomes less sensitive to doping, likely due to reduced charge-transfer character; in contrast, the interlayer exciton exhibits enhanced exciton-charge repulsion. Our results establish hydrostatic pressure as a powerful tuning knob for engineering bosonic quasiparticles and Bose-Fermi interactions in moir\'e materials.

item.title: Magnetic proximity beyond the interface: Layer-sequence-dependent exchange in WSe$_2$/CrI$_3$ heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2610.19582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic proximity effects in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/2D-magnet heterostructures are often described in terms of the magnetization of the interfacial magnetic layer. Here, we show that this picture is sufficient to describe the neutral-exciton valley splitting of the TMD, but incomplete for its hole-doped electronic structure. We study a gate-tunable van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer WSe$_2$ in direct contact with trilayer CrI$_3$. By combining spatially and helicity-resolved reflection-contrast spectroscopy with magnetic circular dichroism, we identify two distinct magnetic domains in the trilayer CrI$_3$: one with purely antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling and one with a mixed antiferromagnetic (AFM)/ferromagnetic~(FM) coupling. In both domains, the sign of the neutral-exciton valley splitting of WSe$_2$ switches with the magnetization reversal of the adjacent CrI$_3$ layer. In contrast, helicity-resolved positive-trion spectroscopy of WSe$_2$ reveals a qualitatively different response. While the AFM domain shows a strongly helicity-selective trion resonance, the mixed AFM/FM domain exhibits trion resonances in both helicities. This behavior disappears when all CrI$_3$ layers are aligned in a parallel magnetization direction. Our results demonstrate that charged excitons are sensitive to the full layer-resolved magnetic sequence of the adjacent 2D-magnet, revealing magnetic proximity beyond the interface.

item.title: Error-controlled switching between discrete and continuum dislocations in a unified defect framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.19841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating defects of every dimension together is expensive, and the savings of adaptive methods are rarely tested at equal accuracy. We present a variational framework in which fields, dislocation lines and defect densities share one free energy, one dissipation law and exact ledgers of mass and Burgers vector, so that a region can change its representation without gaining or losing defects. On this basis, an allocator switches the dislocations themselves between discrete particles, where they are sparse, and a continuous density, where they are dense. The switch is made block by block from local counts, conserves the Burgers vector exactly and is controlled by a single threshold. For $5\times10^5$ dislocations, the allocator reproduces the discrete model to within 1% in the sparse region at 14-37 times lower cost, depending on the machine; the advantage grows to 81 times at $10^6$ dislocations, and a threshold calibrated on one ensemble meets its error target on an independent one. For an idealized array of dislocation walls in copper, the allocator is 37.5 times cheaper than particle dislocation dynamics and, at almost the same cost, six times more accurate than continuum dislocation dynamics between the walls. In a three-dimensional copper model coupling grain-boundary cavitation with damage, ligaments left at nominal coalescence delay creep rupture by 25-48% (post hoc sweep). By contrast, grids refined at interfaces gain less than twofold once the active region exceeds about 30% of the domain, so representation switching, rather than grid refinement, is the effective form of adaptivity for defect-rich microstructures.

item.title: Nonadiabatic polaron dynamics from machine-learned hopping trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2610.19842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The formation and motion of small polarons are ubiquitous in energy materials and influence photoinduced processes. Polaron transport is governed by thermally activated lattice dynamics and rare hopping events, requiring spatial and temporal scales only attainable with machine-learning molecular dynamics, which enables extensive sampling of atomic trajectories and polaron configurations over nanoseconds. Moreover, the Born-Oppenheimer approximation underlying standard ab initio molecular dynamics cannot describe the nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states mediated by nuclear motion, which controls energy exchange and excited-state relaxation. Here, we develop a simulation framework that combines machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to bridge these complementary aspects of polaron physics, and determine how different polaron-hopping mechanisms affect excited-state dynamics. The enlarged trajectory space allows us to provide the first direct dynamical confirmation of the adiabatic or nonadiabatic classification of polaron hopping regimes originally proposed on the basis of static Marcus-theory arguments, and to connect individual hopping events directly to nonadiabatic electronic transitions. In bulk TiO$_2$, nonadiabatic hoppings occur preferentially when the energy of the polaron-induced gap state approaches the conduction-band manifold, promoting both electronic de-excitation and, via a Landau-Zener mechanism, excitation from the ground state. In MgO, the predominantly adiabatic character of hole-polaron hopping suppresses these effects, leading to longer charge-carrier lifetimes and an absence of thermally activated excitations. At the rutile TiO$_2$(110) surface, hopping events are rarer than in bulk because the excess electron is strongly stabilized in the subsurface region, leading to correspondingly longer de-excitation times.

item.title: A practical route to amorphous solid-state electrolyte structures by hybrid reverse Monte Carlo with foundation potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.19846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amorphous alkali oxychlorides are fast ion conductors, but their atomic structure remains unresolved. Total scattering sums all partial pair correlations into one curve that has no unique inversion, so the structure must be modeled. Melt-quench molecular dynamics builds a model from the interatomic potential alone, and reverse Monte Carlo (RMC) builds one from the measurement alone. The two have rarely been compared with all else held fixed. We benchmark both routes and two hybrid schemes on amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}} against one neutron pair distribution function with one foundation potential. The hybrid schemes put the energy either in the acceptance rule (inline) or in short relaxations between blocks of refinement (alternating). Each refinement starts from a melt-quench glass or from a random packing of isolated units. The glass has the lowest energy and places the first-shell peaks correctly, but carries almost none of the oscillation beyond 6~\AA{} (goodness of fit $R^{2} = 0.29$). Pure RMC fits the measurement to within its counting noise ($R^{2} = 0.99$), but at more than $1.3$~eV/atom above the glass, and niobium loses about half of its first-shell chlorine. Started from the glass, both hybrid schemes reach $R^{2} = 0.92$ within $0.1$~eV/atom of its energy and keep its coordination chemistry. Structures from the two inputs fit almost equally well and differ in energy by a tenth of the RMC penalty, yet they differ in whether their polyhedra are connected. The input is therefore part of the method. We recommend quenching a glass with a foundation potential and refining it against the measurement with a hybrid scheme. The resulting structure carries both the local chemistry and the medium-range order, and it is the starting point for modeling ion transport in these conductors.
item.dc:creator: Xintian Wang, Xinyu Zhang, Denys Butenko, Bolong Hong, Jinlong Zhu, Peichen Zhong

item.title: Transverse magneto-gyrotropy driven by spin-induced ferroaxiality
item.description: arXiv:2610.20061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photon chirality is inherently sensitive to structural handedness and magnetism, which break spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetries, respectively. Ferroaxial order, by contrast, hosts two-dimensional chirality while preserving both symmetries, thereby precluding its direct coupling to photon chirality. Intertwining ferroaxiality with magnetic order, however, may lift such constraints and enable unconventional coupling to photon chirality. Nevertheless, the optical response arising from such intertwined order has yet to be demonstrated experimentally. Here, we demonstrate transverse magneto-gyrotropy arising from spin-driven ferroaxiality in the Weyl magnet EuCd2Sb2. Whereas the conventional polar magneto-optical Kerr effect is governed by magnetization parallel to the light-propagation direction, we observe a gyrotropic response associated with magnetization transverse to the light-propagation direction. The optical rotation exhibits a characteristic 120-degree periodicity upon rotation of the in-plane magnetic field, reflecting the threefold symmetry of the emergent ferroaxial state and revealing the ferroaxial origin of the transverse gyrotropic response. This coupling to photon chirality enables vectorial control of the gyrotropic response through the magnetic field direction. Our findings establish an interaction between photon chirality and transverse magnetization enabled by intertwined ferroaxial and magnetic orders, demonstrating a novel form of multiferroicity with functional light-matter interaction.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihiro Okamura, Takumi Kagawa, Ayano Nakamura, Shinichi Nishihaya, Masaki Uchida, Susumu Minami, Ryotaro Arita, Youtarou Takahashi

item.title: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.20063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Defect engineering is a crucial tool for tuning and tailoring the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials. A key challenge is identifying which defects are kinetically stable at room temperature and sufficiently promising to warrant further investigation. However, identifying stable defects with suitable properties using first-principles calculations, such as density functional theory (DFT) is computationally demanding, effectively limiting the scope of high-throughput studies. In this work, we investigate whether the machine learning interatomic potential MACE can reproduce sorption trends (adsorption vs. absorption) previously obtained from high-throughput DFT calculations and extend the analysis to elevated temperatures. A total of 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database are simulated using MACE-accelerated molecular dynamics (MD) at both 0 K and 300 K. The results show that MACE successfully reproduces the overall sorption trends observed in DFT calculations at 0 K at a fraction of the computational cost. Simulations performed at 300 K further indicate that the qualitative sorption trends remain largely the same when including finite-temperature effects. These findings demonstrate that MACE-driven MD can be used as an effective high-throughput prescreening tool for defect-related studies in 2D materials, specially related to sorption. While conventional first-principles methods, such as DFT, remain necessary for accurate and quantitative validation, the use of MLIPs enables MD simulations of finite-temperature defect behavior at a fraction of the computational cost of DFT-based MD.
item.dc:creator: Nils-Ruben Skogemyr, Albin Sj\"ostedt, Isak Wernroth, Isak H\"aggqvist, Isac Ljungwald, Hans-Ove {\AA}kesson, Henricus R. A. ten Eikelder, Rickard Armiento, Joel Davidsson

item.title: Identification of carbon-related color centers in hBN by high-resolution ab initio photoluminescence modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.20127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identification of optically active defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) remains challenging because different defect candidates can produce similar calculated photoluminescence (PL) lineshapes. Here, we demonstrate that force-constant embedding methodology can be extended to calculate high-resolution, vibrationally resolved PL lineshapes in the polar layered material hBN. Benchmarking against the carbon dimer defect, responsible for the 4.1 eV emission, we show that the methodology accurately reproduces the low-energy acoustic phonons and fine spectral features that are inaccessible when using direct supercell calculations. Applying the methodology to neutral carbon trimers ($\mathrm{C_2 C_B}$ and $\mathrm{C_2 C_N}$), we find that the calculated PL lineshape and excitation energy of $\mathrm{C_2 C_N}$ closely match the low-temperature spectrum of the emitter with a zero-phonon line at 1.54 eV. These results establish high-resolution phonon-sideband modeling as a powerful tool for discriminating among candidate defects in polar materials.
item.dc:creator: Vytautas \v{Z}alandauskas, Marek Maciaszek, Marianne Etzelm\"uller Bathen, Julius Janu\v{s}onis, Tadas Paulauskas, Lukas Razinkovas

item.title: Access Rate-Dependent Endurance Behavior of Ferroelectric Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Capacitors
item.description: arXiv:2610.20154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorite-structured ferroelectrics, such as hafnium zirconium oxide ($Hf_{1-x}Zr_{x}O_{2}$), are among the most promising materials for developing the next generation of low-power nonvolatile memories. Emulating realistic operating scenarios for ferroelectric memories requires performing access rate-dependent endurance tests. The access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization cannot be described as a mere superposition of fatigue and imprint effects, which are observed in conventional endurance and retention tests, respectively. The interplay between these degradation mechanisms and its correlation with the delay time in between the programming pulses remains unclear. Combining electrical testing through voltage pulses with ab initio and drift-diffusion simulations provides a comprehensive perspective on the microscopic origin of the access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization of ferroelectric capacitors based on product-relevant 5 nm thick $Hf_{0.5}Zr_{0.5}O_{2}$ films. The role of oxygen vacancy defects accumulating at the electrode-ferroelectric interface with delay time in reducing the fraction of switchable domains is elucidated considering electron transfer processes which change the defect charge state. Building upon this theoretical understanding, a physics-based model to extrapolate the long-term access rate-dependent endurance performance is developed and experimentally verified for temperatures up to 135{\deg}C and delay times up to 2 ms.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Guido, Julie Laguerre, Pramoda Vishnumurthy, Florian Wunderwald, Kristina Holsgrove, Thomas Mikolajick, Sou-Chi Chang, Alfred Kersch, Uwe Schroeder

item.title: High-Frequency Mass Transfer Enabling Over-Limiting Currents in Porous Electrodes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. However, over-limiting currents (OLCs), which exceed this limit, are often observed and have been attributed to surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic effects. Here, we use a frequency-domain framework to identify a different mechanism governed by the time scale of concentration variation. For perfectly reactive interfaces, the spectral Sherwood number, a frequency-dependent dimensionless measure of interfacial mass transfer relative to molecular diffusion, grows as $\Shnd\sim\omega^{1/2}$ at high frequency, while its phase approaches $\pi/4$. This response corresponds to the semi-infinite Warburg limit of the electrochemical impedance. A scaling analysis shows that the exponent and prefactor are determined by diffusion within a thin layer adjacent to the interface and are therefore independent of the global pore geometry. Numerical results for parallel plates, circular tubes, and twelve porous microstructures confirm this scaling. Geometry, flow strength, and flow direction affect the low-frequency response and crossover frequency, but not the asymptotic scaling in the high-frequency limit. This temporal route to OLCs requires neither surface charge nor confinement and could inform the design of systems for pulsed electrodeposition, mineral recovery and renewable-energy storage.
item.dc:creator: Md Abdul Hamid, Kyle C. Smith

item.title: A Topological\-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for Scalable and Interpretable Modeling of Two\-Dimensional Carbon Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a compact Topological-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for planar two-dimensional carbon networks. Atomic coordinates are mapped to a periodic planar graph and represented through ring populations, topological-charge statistics, projected ring geometry, and dual-graph defect adjacency. The resulting modeling vector contains 19 physically interpretable features. We evaluate TGD on 120 published planar carbon allotropes using the DFT relative energy per atom with respect to graphene as the target. Repeated five-fold cross-validation with gradient boosting yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0826 +/- 0.0138 eV/atom and R2 = 0.803 +/- 0.074. Under the same validation protocol, TGD gives a mean MAE of 0.0828 eV/atom, compared with 0.0929 eV/atom for a 203-feature Matminer representation. We further analyze 360 vacancy-defected graphene configurations spanning 12 vacancy concentrations from 2 to 24 percent. When entire vacancy concentrations are held out, TGD gives a pooled MAE of 0.269 eV/vacancy and R2 = 0.861, outperforming simple baselines based on vacancy concentration alone or non-hexagonal-ring fraction alone. Sensitivity tests show that the inferred edge sets are stable to moderate changes in the adaptive bond factor. Finally, the mean absolute topological charge is examined as a one-variable empirical surrogate for the allotrope dataset and is treated explicitly as dataset-specific rather than universal. These results show that TGD combines compact prediction with direct structural interpretation while making clear the present restriction to single-layer planar carbon networks.
item.dc:creator: R\^omulo Uriel Liberal de Oliveira, Raphael Matozo Tromer

item.title: Modeling electrodeposition of thin films with compact, dendritic, and random morphologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.20361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We summarize previously published computer simulation studies of a metal electrodeposition model that considers diffusive cation flux, a fast reaction in contact with the electrode or with the growing deposit, and adsorbed atom diffusion in finite time windows. Simulations with various parameters show compact, fractal, dendritic deposits, and dynamic transitions between different morphologies during the growth of individual samples. The dendritic shapes are characterized by hierarchical organizations in which branches of a given order reproduce the shape and crystalline orientation of the branches of the previous order, in contrast to the random branching of the fractal deposits formed by DLA and related models. The simulations show dendrites with maple leaf shape in SC lattices, pine tree shape in FCC lattices, and flower-like shape in HCP lattices, with surfaces predominantly oriented in the lowest-energy configurations of each lattice. Simulations with nucleation restricted to a nanoscale seed show the initial formation of faceted particles followed by dendrite formation, in agreement with silver electrodeposition on substrates patterned with gold nanoparticles. A quantitative application to faceted and dendritic silver obtained in the same experiment provides values of the model parameters which are consistent with the characteristic widths of these structures being of the same order of magnitude of the diffusion lengths of atoms on (111) and (001) surfaces. Using an extended model for iron electrodeposition on Si(100), the simulations qualitatively reproduce the initial formation of multilayer islands, small oscillations of the roughness of a polycrystalline compact film after island coalescence, and instability development. Possible directions for applying this modeling to the electrodeposition of other materials are suggested.
item.dc:creator: F\'abio D. A. Aar\~ao Reis, Dung di Caprio, Sidiney G. Alves, Ismael S. S. Carrasco

item.title: Structural identification in general crystalline systems via Voronoi cell topology
item.description: arXiv:2610.20498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Widely used methods for identifying crystal structure in atomistic simulations are limited in practice to a handful of simple structures, leaving many important crystalline systems without automated classification techniques. Voronoi topology analysis offers a route to classifying arbitrary crystalline and defect environments, but realizing this potential first requires enumerating the Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under thermal perturbation of a structure of interest. We present an algorithm that deterministically enumerates all Voronoi cell topologies arising from generic infinitesimal perturbations of an arbitrary crystal structure, producing structural classifiers that extend automated identification to general crystalline systems. We demonstrate the approach on several structures of general interest.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel A. Lazar, Chris H. Rycroft

item.title: Growth-induced trade-off between polarity, electrical isolation, and structural quality in AlN grown on Si(111) by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy
item.description: arXiv:2610.20523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the effects of substrate temperature and Al flux, at a fixed N flux, on the polarity, electrical properties, and structural quality of AlN films grown on high-resistivity Si(111) by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. N-rich conditions result in relatively highly resistive Al-polar AlN/Si, whereas Al-rich conditions promote N-polarity and improved structural quality but simultaneously lead to increased p-type conductivity of AlN/Si stacks, consistent with unintentional Al doping of the Si substrate during AlN growth. Increasing the substrate temperature further improves the structural quality while enhancing the unwanted conductivity, revealing a growth-induced trade-off among polarity, electrical isolation, and structural quality. By reducing the substrate temperature to 575{\deg}C while maintaining slightly Al-rich conditions, an N-polar AlN/Si stack with a sheet resistance of 276 k{\Omega}/sq is achieved. These results provide guidelines for optimizing AlN/Si templates for various nitride device heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Hossein Yazdani, Nhu Tran, Xin Du, Vit Hornik, Roman Gr\"oger, YongJin Cho

item.title: Exchange Interactions and Magnon Spectra in bcc Fe(001) Thin Films: A Computational Study
item.description: arXiv:2610.20564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We combined density functional theory with atomistic spin dynamics to understand how surfaces influence magnon dispersion. For this purpose, we investigate thin layers of body-centered cubic iron and compare them with the bulk material. We present how the broken symmetry affects exchange interactions and magnon behavior. Our results reveal enhanced magnetic moments and exchange interactions for surface atoms compared to bulk Fe. The increase in exchange interaction integrals is mostly visible for first- and second-nearest neighbors. We also find a significant spread in exchange values within each coordination shell. Magnon dispersion analysis shows, for the layered system, pronounced band blurring, a significant reduction of maximum frequencies relative to the previously reported bulk values, and the emergence of a low-frequency band outside the \g{}-point. Our study shows that relying on bulk exchange parameters introduces errors in the magnon spectra of ultrathin systems, underscoring the need for a detailed, system-specific approach.
item.dc:creator: Joanna Marciniak, Wojciech Marciniak, Jorge Luis Brise\~no-G\'omez, Jan Rusz

item.title: Supercell-enabled inverse design of boundary-state dispersion for group-velocity control in pseudomagnetic phononic crystals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological boundary states offer a platform for guided-wave propagation within bulk bandgaps. Their propagation characteristics depend not only on the spectral extent of the states but also on their dispersion within the operating bandwidth. A nearly linear dispersion provides more uniform group velocity across frequency, whereas a reduced slope enables slow-wave propagation. Despite advances in inverse design of prescribed dispersion relations and topological dispersion tuning, application-oriented characteristics of boundary-state dispersion have rarely been direct inverse-design objectives. Here, we develop a supercell-enabled, surrogate-assisted framework for the inverse design of boundary-state dispersion in a phononic crystal with pseudomagnetic fields. Area-preserving anisotropic deformation shifts the local Dirac points, and independent variation of 21 rows within the supercell provides distributed control over the boundary-state branch. A constraint-preserving surrogate reconstructs the dispersion from an initial frequency and positive frequency increments, with first- and second-difference losses introduced to capture local slope and curvature. Coupled with a genetic algorithm, the framework targets two prescribed-bandwidth design tasks: highly linear dispersion and slow-wave dispersion. For the former, finite-element verification yields relative group-velocity variations of 0.142% to 1.183% over prescribed bandwidths of 4% to 6%. For slow-wave designs, mean group velocities of 190 to 385 m/s are obtained over bandwidths of 0.2% to 0.8% while satisfying a 5% group-velocity variation limit. These results establish boundary-state dispersion as a direct inverse-design target beyond conventional bandwidth optimization, opening a flexible route to group-velocity control through application-oriented dispersion engineering over prescribed relative bandwidths.
item.dc:creator: Hua-Yang Chen, Nan-Xin Yu, Zhen-Hui Qin, Yan-Feng Chen, Si-Yuan Yu

item.title: Topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals
item.description: arXiv:2610.19017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metals with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing. In the minimal bilayer system, interlayer tunneling reconstructs the spin-split Fermi surfaces and generates two layer-hybridized sectors with distinct effective chemical potentials. Without Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), the emergent mirror symmetry and subsystem chiral symmetry stabilize phases with different numbers of helical Majorana edge-mode pairs and additional counterpropagating pairs, jointly characterized by the mirror Chern number and the winding numbers defined along high-symmetry lines. The combination of RSOC and the altermagnetic exchange field gaps out the helical Majorana pairs while, in a certain parameter regime, leaving another pair of counterpropagating Majorana edge modes gapless, giving rise to second-order topological phases with isolated or twofold Majorana corner modes, as well as a hybrid-order phase in which gapless Majorana edge modes coexist with Majorana corner modes. We identify a layer symmetry that elucidates the physical origin of these phases. For an arbitrary N-layer system, such a symmetry naturally arises from the interlayer-coupling matrix, allowing N-fold Majorana corner modes to emerge when all layer-hybridized sectors enter the nontrivial second-order regime. Our results establish the interplay among the layer degree of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface configurations as a controllable route to engineering topological superconductivity in layered altermagnetic systems.

item.title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for PHREEQC-Coupled Reactive Transport with Cell-Based Surface Complexation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a mass-conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes (DBS) formulation for reactive transport with cell-based surface complexation in image-based porous media, coupled to PHREEQC and implemented in GeoChemFoam, an OpenFOAM-based toolbox. Dissolved species are transported in the physical mobile-water fraction, adsorbed species are stored as conservative cell-scale surface inventories, and each reactive cell is coupled to PHREEQC. Reactive surface area is prescribed independently as a cell field, so that internal area left unresolved by segmentation of microporous phases can be represented while DBS flow and transport are retained in the resolved pore space. The implementation is verified with a test suite that isolates the coupling of transport and chemistry from the construction of reactive surface area. Aqueous and adsorbed mass balance is evaluated against a one-dimensional analytical retardation benchmark and closed-system batch calculations. The smooth-interface surface-area algorithms are tested on idealised two- and three-dimensional geometries. In a two-scale lithium micromodel, DBS reproduces fully resolved aqueous and sorbed inventories within 0.6% across Pe=0.1-10. The applications comprise Pb2+ retardation by hydrous ferric oxide coatings in a two-dimensional fracture network, competitive Mn2+/Mg2+ exchange in a three-dimensional Kelvin-cell sorbent, and Sr2+/Ca2+ exchange in Estaillades limestone. In the fracture-network and limestone cases, the formulation yields spatially resolved aqueous and adsorbed inventories even where reactive surface area is only partly resolved at the image scale. The framework therefore supports conservative surface-complexation modelling in both resolved and unresolved pore structures, with relevance to contaminant retention, selective ion capture, and radionuclide transport.

item.title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
item.description: arXiv:2610.19195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Zhongkai Tao, Mengxuan Yang

item.title: On the Mathematical Structure of Helical Shear in Anelastic Continua
item.description: arXiv:2610.19221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study helical shear of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid carrying a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations. Through the Bilby--Kr\"oner--Lee decomposition, the dislocations are encoded in a Weitzenb\"ock material manifold, whose Riemannian metric alone enters the elastic response. Equilibrium reduces at each radius to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, whose cross terms are proportional to the dislocation strength and to the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant; the two shear modes therefore couple only in the presence of dislocations. Exact solutions are obtained for neo-Hookean, Fung--Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney--Rivlin materials, and numerical ones for Gent--Gent materials. The universal relations of Horgan and Saccomandi are extended to dislocated generalized neo-Hookean tubes. Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, couple the two shear modes chirally when it depends on the second, and may restrict admissibility: they cap the dislocation strength in Gent and Gent--Gent materials, and contract the admissible traction region in Knowles materials with power-law index below n = 1/2. A weakly nonlinear analysis to third order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength shows that, at first order (linear elasticity), the dislocations leave the shear response unaffected while carrying a residual stress. The chiral coupling enters at second order, through the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant, so that every dislocated material couples the modes as the Mooney--Rivlin solid with the same second- and third-order moduli. At third order, no new coupling arises; the modes interact through stiffness corrections involving the fourth-order modulus, which the dislocations further correct mode by mode.

item.title: Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
item.description: arXiv:2610.19269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodic solids with strongly interacting electrons display phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories and the associated frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. We showcase this perspective by studying the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model. We find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet displays, in addition to stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy of the self-energy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such an intricate many-body state: the pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and the metallic interfaces, which echoes the role of spin-fluctuations identified by nonperturbative methods.

item.title: Signatures of symmetry-stabilized Dirac fermions in correlated oxide CaNbO3 thin films
item.description: arXiv:2610.19276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry-protected electronic states in correlated oxides offer a route to combining topology, lattice tunability, and many-body interactions, but creating such topological electronic states in complex oxides remains challenging. Here, we show that oxygen octahedral rotations provide a symmetry-control parameter for stabilizing Dirac-related electronic states in epitaxial CaNbO3 films. By comparing compressively strained tetragonal films and relaxed orthorhombic films, we demonstrate that distinct octahedral rotation patterns preserve nonsymmorphic symmetry and lead to distinct transport signatures consistent with Dirac-like electronic states. The films exhibit metallic transport with high mobility of 138,000 cm2 V-1 s-1, multichannel conduction, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations from small high-mobility Fermi pockets. Landau-fan diagram analysis indicates finite Berry-phase contributions, while first-principles calculations reveal a strain-driven evolution from nodal-line band crossings in the orthorhombic phase to Dirac-electron band features in the tetragonal phase. These results establish oxygen octahedral symmetry as a design knob for engineering topological electronic states in correlated perovskite oxides.

item.title: Evidence for hidden order and its potential correlation with electron-hole asymmetry in iridate superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.19334v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hidden order refers to an order that shapes the properties of quantum materials yet remains difficult to identify. Here we report signatures of a hidden order in doped iridate superlattices through an unexpected electron-hole asymmetry in the coupling between the insulating state and the antiferromagnetic (AFM) state. While carrier doping suppresses both states, they remain coupled in the electron-doped regime but decouple in the hole-doped regime. Structural analysis rules out octahedral rotation and tilting as the dominant origin of this asymmetry. Instead, magnetic characterization reveals evidences of a hidden order that only appears in the hole-doped regime. This hidden order emerges above TN and is closely associated with the AFM state, coinciding with an exceptionally strong magnetic scattering intensity and an anomalously robust magnetic coherence. Our results highlight that hole-doped iridates can be a promising platform for exploring hidden and unconventional ordering phenomena in spin-orbit-entangled quantum materials.

item.title: Seismology of Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.19602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aging and relaxation of glasses proceed through localized rearrangements that also generate long-ranged mechanical responses in their surroundings. We develop a theory that treats these rearrangements as internal microseismic sources, and thereby separates the direct effects emerging from an event from the effects from the far-field displacements it generates. These far-field disturbances propagate and relax through the viscoelastic medium through which they move, producing a stochastic background of weak but numerous perturbations at any given location. Combining the description of local events from the Random First Order Transition theory with this propagating background, we derive a unified equation for the dynamical structure factor of a relaxing glass. The theory identifies a finite wave-vector and time window in which the growing viscoelastic far-field disturbances can produce compressed exponential relaxation, which has been observed using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy. At higher wave vectors that resolve local jumps, heterogeneity of the local event dynamics instead produces stretched exponential relaxation. The crossover between these behaviors depends on the event statistics and the scattering phase accumulated across the region reached through viscoelastic propagation from the numerous distant sources.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Cao, Peter G. Wolynes

item.title: Emergent medium-range order in amorphous silicon
item.description: arXiv:2610.19620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medium-range order (MRO) is an important feature of amorphous materials, but its nature in terms of atomic arrangement has remained elusive. Here, using large-scale machine-learning-driven atomistic simulations of amorphous silicon, we probe the MRO of this archetypal network glass. By characterizing the structure in three dimensions, we reveal that the symmetry of the atomic arrangement around a central atom shows a crossover as a function of distance. At short distances, the structure is determined by local bonding constraints, which evolve from predominantly tetrahedral environments in low-density amorphous silicon to highly coordinated and strongly disordered local environments in very-high-density amorphous silicon. At larger distances, however, distinct cubic- and octahedral-symmetry patterns emerge in the three-dimensional atomic-density distribution, despite the absence of these symmetries at shorter length scales. We find that this crossover is accompanied by a quasi-periodic spatial organization of the topological rings in the structure. The characteristic spacing between ring centers matches the length scale of the first sharp diffraction peak (FSDP) in the structure factor, establishing a direct connection between this reciprocal-space signature of MRO and its real-space organization. These results demonstrate that the FSDP, the spatial correlation of the rings, and emergent orientational symmetries are not independent manifestations of MRO, but reflect different aspects of a common structural organization. Our findings provide a unified real-space picture of MRO in amorphous silicon and suggest that intermediate-range structural order in network glasses emerges from the interplay between local bonding constraints and extended atomic arrangements driven by efficient packing.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Zhang, Stephen R. Elliott, Yujie Wang, Walter Kob

item.title: Room-Temperature Metallic 2D Ferromagnetism Stabilized by Quantum Metric
item.description: arXiv:2610.19713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The recent discovery of long-sought dice-lattice bands in layered electride YCl opens up unprecedented opportunities for studying correlated electrons in real dice lattice systems. While the weakly dispersive band at the Fermi level is partially filled and density-wave states are expected due to Fermi surface nesting based on conventional theories, the ARPES measurement nevertheless revealed a uniform flat band splitting of 0.5 eV, suggesting unusual ferromagnetism (FM) borne out of the metallic 2D dice lattice. In this Letter, we propose that the uniform metallic FM order is stabilized by the prominent quantum metric near topological band crossing points at K and K', which reconstructs the magnetic instability in the dice metal and tips the density-wave instability toward a uniform FM order. Importantly, our analysis based on random phase approximation (RPA) and Hartree-Fock theory predicts a remarkably high Curie temperature above room temperature for the 2D FM order. These findings establish the first example of a room-temperature 2D metallic magnet stabilized by quantum metric, which not only exemplifies the fundamental significance of quantum geometry in solids but also bears far-reaching applications in energy-efficient high-density magnetic memories.
item.dc:creator: Teng-Fei Ying, Jianqi Zhong, Songyuan Geng, Fangjie Chen, Haoxiang Li, Benjamin T. Zhou

item.title: Beyond Kitaev exchange: $\Gamma'$-driven magnetism in Ag$_3$LiRh$_2$O$_6$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Kitaev magnets, frustration arises from bond-dependent spin anisotropic interactions, which can potentially realize sought-after quantum spin liquid phases. However, material realizations with dominating Kitaev exchange are scarce and the broad parameter space of extended Kitaev models remains largely unexplored experimentally. Here, we use density-functional theory, cluster many-body, spin-wave, and density-matrix renormalization calculations to show that the recently discovered honeycomb rhodate Ag$_3$LiRh$_2$O$_6$ hosts an off-diagonal exchange $\Gamma_1'$ that is second in magnitude only to the ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $K_1$. This combination of $K_1$ and $\Gamma_1'$ explains key experimental observations, an unusually high magnetic ordering temperature of 94 K at ambient pressure and its rapid decrease under hydrostatic pressure as Ag$_3$LiRh$_2$O$_6$ evolves from ferromagnetic toward zigzag order within the honeycomb planes. Our spin-wave calculations further predict an unusual topology of the magnon bands arising from the $\Gamma_1'$ term in the spin Hamiltonian of the honeycomb layer. We show that the large trigonal splitting of $t_{2g}$ states enhances $\Gamma_1'$, the hitherto underappreciated term in Kitaev magnets, and opens the way to new interesting regimes of the extended Kitaev model.

item.title: Magnetic field induced modulation of heat transport in CrPS$_4$ probed by TaIrTe$_4$ transverse Seebeck thermometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.19833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding and controlling heat flow in low-dimensional magnetic materials is central to thermoelectrics and spin caloritronics. One of the challenges is the absence of sensitive probes of small, field-dependent modulations in thermal transport. Here we demonstrate transverse Seebeck thermometry using exfoliated TaIrTe$_4$ as a probe of thermal conductivity modulated by an external magnetic field on a van der Waals magnet, CrPS$_4$. With a temperature gradient oriented at $45^\circ$ to its principal crystallographic axes, TaIrTe$_4$ exhibits a transverse thermopower exceeding $200~\mathrm{\mu V\,K^{-1}}$ for 900 nm wide and 30 $\mu$m long electrodes, enabling precise detection of variations in the local temperature gradients. Exploiting this with CrPS$_4$ in a nonlocal geometry, we resolve distinct field dependent thermal conductivity changes associated with both the spin-flip and spin-flop magnetic transitions which we attribute to variations in the magnon$-$phonon coupling in CrPS$_4$. At 5 K, the transverse Seebeck response is modulated by more than 8$\%$ by an external magnetic field, demonstrating strong magnetic control of heat transport in CrPS$_4$. This all van der Waals platform offers high sensitivity to modulations of thermal conductivity and a broad adaptability to a wide range of exfoliated magnetic systems.

item.title: Andreev-reflection spectroscopy of SrPt3P single crystals
item.description: arXiv:2610.19851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interplay between inversion symmetry breaking and superconducting pairing mechanisms is a long-standing puzzle of solid-state physics. Ternary platinum phosphide SrPt$_3$P is an excellent case study in this regard, since it shares the distorted anti-perovskite crystal structure of non-centrosymmetric superconductor CePt$_3$Si but preserves the inversion symmetry center, enabling a direct comparison between the two compounds. Despite intense scrutiny, the superconducting pairing strength, gap symmetry, and magnitude of SrPt$_3$P remain an open question. Here, we study the gap structure of high-quality SrPt$_3$P single crystals with $T_c = 8.6$ K by using point-contact Andreev-reflection spectroscopy. The spectra systematically showed symmetric conductance maxima and a zero-bias minimum, as is typical of fully gapped superconductors, and dips at finite voltage $V_\mathrm{dip}$ due to the local transition of the contact region to the resistive state. In contacts with high resistance, where the dips fall sufficiently far from the gap features, the conductance curves can be well fitted with a single isotropic $s$-wave gap. The temperature dependence $\Delta(T)$ of the gap amplitude extracted from the fit is in good agreement with the one predicted by the BCS theory, with a zero-temperature mean value $\Delta(0)=1.88\pm0.08$ meV, and a mean gap ratio $2\Delta/k_\mathrm{B}T_c = 5.2\pm0.2$.
item.dc:creator: Valeriy A. Stepanov, Nikolai D. Zhigadlo, Erik Piatti, Dario Daghero

item.title: Beyond DFT electronic band structures via dual-space orbital learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.19919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate electronic band structures are essential for predicting material properties, but high-fidelity calculations are computationally demanding. We introduce O-kRystal, a dual-space orbital-learning framework that uses a lower-cost Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) calculation as both an energy baseline and a source of structured orbital information. Combining PBE band energies with real- and reciprocal-space orbital matrices, O-kRystal predicts higher-level corrections for individual electronic states as a function of crystal momentum and spin. For states within 5 eV of the band-edge midpoint, it predicts Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof (HSE06) band energies with a mean absolute error of $0.171 \pm 0.009$ eV across nearly 6,000 three-dimensional materials spanning insulating, metallic, magnetic, and nonmagnetic systems. On a separate benchmark of six strongly correlated materials, it reduces the corresponding PBE band-energy MAE by 68.7% and resolves orbital-dependent changes in the relative placement of transition-metal d and ligand p states. Despite training only at high-symmetry points, it maintains comparable accuracy at unseen points along band paths and reconstructs HSE06 densities of states from dense Brillouin-zone predictions. Finally, training O-kRystal on $G_0W_0$ quasiparticle energies for two-dimensional materials demonstrates its applicability across levels of theory and the potential of orbital learning for higher-fidelity, momentum-resolved electronic-structure prediction beyond density functional theory.
item.dc:creator: Minhyuk Kang, Beom Seok Kang, Nikolai Argatoff, Miguel Nouman, Danish Khan, William A. Goddard III, Anima Anandkumar

item.title: High-Harmonic Generation Probes Quantum Nuclear Fluctuations in Liquid Water
item.description: arXiv:2610.19967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nuclear quantum effects are essential for an accurate description of the hydrogen-bonded structure of liquid water, yet their spectroscopic signatures can be subtle and difficult to measure. Moreover, probing these effects in solution on femtosecond timescales (or below) is an open challenge that is pivotal for optical control of hydrogen bonds and ultrafast spectroscopy of proton transfer. Here, we combine path-integral molecular dynamics with real-time time-dependent density-functional theory to explore high-harmonic generation (HHG) in liquid water from first principles, rigorously accounting for quantum nuclear delocalisation. Relative to classical-nuclei simulations, quantum sampling suppresses the harmonic yield around certain harmonics by up to an order of magnitude, inducing local structural minima. By analysing the ab initio simulations and reproducing the key effects with a simplified model Hamiltonian, we trace the physical origins of the interference minima to the broadening of valence-band states induced by hydrogen-bond fluctuations, a mechanism expected to generalise to other hydrogen-bonded structures. Our work shows that nuclear quantum effects are indispensable for capturing ultrafast electronic dynamics in liquids, and demonstrates the power of liquid HHG spectroscopy for attosecond probing of nuclear fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: George Trenins, Nicolas Tancogne-Dejean, Angana Mondal, Angel Rubio, Hans Jakob W\"orner, Aaron Kelly, Ofer Neufeld, Mariana Rossi

item.title: Polaritonic self-hybridized critical coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Maximizing the absorption of exciton-polaritons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) under critical coupling conditions is crucial for developing high-efficiency polariton-based photodetectors, solar cells, and perfect absorbers. Here, we propose a polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding driven quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBIC) mode and A excitons in a bulk WS2 metasurface. This polaritonic critical coupling shows robust behavior with respect to the asymmetric parameters of the involved BZF-QBIC mode, in contrast to the asymmetry-sensitive conventional QBIC-based critical coupling. By changing the height of WS2 metasurfaces, we observe a typical anti-crossing behavior with a Rabi splitting of 246.5 meV. Moreover, the maximum absorption value of 0.5 for exciton-polaritons is achieved at the polaritonic critical coupling condition. The large population of excitons provided by bulk WS2 is essential for achieving polaritonic critical coupling and can further enhance polaritonic absorption. This work enables the realization of robust, high-absorption self-hybridized polaritonic critical coupling in TMDCs, and further expedite their applications in high-absorption low-dimensional polaritonic devices.
item.dc:creator: Kuidong Wang, Xiongwei Guo, Fu Liu, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou

item.title: Bulk superconductivity in quintuple-layer square-planar nickelate La6Ni5O12
item.description: arXiv:2610.20249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nickelate superconductors, sharing a similar electronic environment with cuprate superconductors, offer a promising platform for unraveling the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. However, the realization of superconductivity in these systems has so far been restricted to thin films or bulk samples under high-pressure. This limits the applicability of various experimental probes to study the mechanism of superconductivity, and hinders the potential application of the nickelate superconductors. Exploring bulk superconductivity at ambient pressure is therefore essential to understand its origin and enable broader experimental research. Here, we report the realization of bulk superconductivity at ambient-pressure in quintuple-layer square-planar (SP) nickelate La6Ni5O12. The SP phase is obtained by performing topotactic reaction on the quintuple-layer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) compound La6Ni5O16. Optimized reduction condition endows La6Ni5O12 with a superconducting state that exhibits onset transition temperature of ~ 18 K, as verified by both zero resistance and diamagnetic shielding effect. Pronounced hysteresis loops revealed by magnetization and torque magnetometry demonstrate the occurrence of vortex pinning. Specific heat measurements on a polycrystalline pellet of La6Ni5O12 reveal a clear superconducting transition at ~18 K and a superconducting volume fraction of ~ 25%, which strongly supports the presence of bulk superconductivity. Our results establish an unprecedented bulk sample platform for investigating superconductivity in nickelates at ambient pressure, which paves the way for further experimental studies into the superconducting mechanism.

item.title: Landau quantization of $C_3$ high-fold fermions in honeycomb lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.20595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the theory of the Landau levels of $C_3$ high-fold fermions in honeycomb lattices. These fermions arise as a generalization of the tight-binding model in a honeycomb lattice with one orbital per site, known to describe graphene, to a family of models with several orbitals per site transforming according to representations of $C_3$, relevant for triangulene two-dimensional crystals. The models are defined by the number of orbitals $n_a$ and $n_b$ at the $a$ and $b$ sites of the unit cell. They feature energy bands that combine flat bands and Dirac cones, that are isomorphic to those of graphene, the Lieb, $p_{xy}$ honeycomb, and the Kagome tight-binding models. Combining tight-binding and $k\cdot p$ methods, here we compute the Landau levels of the $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,2)$ and $(3,3)$ models, we compare them to those of the reference models, and we explore the similarities and differences with the Landau levels in graphene. Our findings reveal that the nature of $C_3$ high-fold fermions combine Dirac-type Landau quantization, originating from the linear crossings and associated relativistic band dispersion, with anomalous Landau quantization rooted in the quantum geometry of the singular flat bands.
item.dc:creator: Luisa Madail, Joaqu\'in Fern\'andez-Rossier

item.title: Magnetic Structures Database from Symmetry-aided High-Throughput Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2601.01617v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic structures-the spatial arrangement of magnetic moments-underpin the diverse functionalities of magnetic materials, yet they have been experimentally determined for only a small fraction of known compounds. Conventional first-principles prediction requires candidate magnetic configurations as input, but the number of possible configurations is in principle infinite. Although the classic Landau-theory based symmetry analysis is widely used to classify magnetic ordering, their direct application to generate input magnetic configurations remains a major challenge due to unavoidable residual degrees of freedom. Here we turn this classification language into a practical predictive framework by resolving these freedoms through a two-step symmetry-aided strategy: an irrep-compatible maximal-magnetic-subgroup selection, followed by the physically motivated high-symmetry-direction construction. This highly efficient scheme is justified within the newly developed oriented spin space group framework. Benchmarked against 1,043 Landau-compatible experimental structures in MAGNDATA, our candidate sets reproduce 90% of the experimentally reported magnetic structures in the four high-symmetry crystal systems with only ~51 candidates per material on average, and subsequent first-principles calculations with material-specific Hubbard U parameters recover the experimental ground state with 83% accuracy. Applying the validated workflow to 19,808 transition-metal compounds, we construct a database of more than 5,000 magnetic materials-nearly twice the size of the experimental MAGNDATA. The database reveals statistical regularities accessible only at scale, including the occurrence rate of magnetism, the prevalence of competing magnetic states, and enables the identification of hundreds of magnetic topological materials, altermagnets, and other emerging magnetic phases and functionalities.

item.title: Fluctuation-driven multi-step charge density wave melting in monolayer TiSe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2604.20355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The exact microscopic origin, symmetry, and thermal melting mechanism of the charge density wave (CDW) phase in TiSe$_2$ remain intensely debated, particularly regarding chiral structural order and multi-step phase transitions. Using large-scale molecular dynamics driven by an accurate machine-learning interatomic potential, we resolve the finite-temperature structural dynamics of the monolayer TiSe$_2$. We demonstrate that CDW melting deviates from conventional mean-field second-order behavior, undergoing a two-step process characterized by an extended fluctuation region ($200-250$ K) with proliferating domain walls, phase decoherence, component-selective melting, and an overdamped soft optical phonon. Furthermore, anisotropic long-wavelength thermal fluctuations spontaneously stabilize an asymmetric $3Q$ CDW order with $P1$ symmetry. These findings provide a unified microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven transitions in 2D quantum materials, demonstrating that the complex CDW physics of TiSe$_2$ is captured entirely via non-perturbative electron-phonon and phonon-phonon interactions.
item.dc:creator: Luka Beni\'c, Dino Novko, Ivor Lon\v{c}ari\'c

item.title: Vacancy-Enhanced $N-N$ Bonding and Deep Level Complex Defect Formation in $\beta-Ga_2O_3$
item.description: arXiv:2605.12029v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nitrogen implantation can make $\beta-Ga_2O_3$ semi-insulating, but the atomic origin responsible for carrier trapping remains unresolved. Here, hybrid density functional theory is used to examine complexes derived from an interstitial-substitutional N pair, $N_{i9}-N_{OI}$, and effects of nearby O and Ga vacancies on $N-N$ bonding, stability, and electronic states. Within the configurations examined, N atoms favor co-localization. In selected Ga-vacancy-assisted complexes, the $N-N$ distance shortens to 1.09-1.19 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ and exhibits electron localization consistent with substantial $N-N$ covalent character. Positive binding energies indicate favorable association relative to separated defects, although many of these complexes have high formation energies and are therefore more likely to be metastable products of implantation than abundant equilibrium defects. Calculated N $K$-edge XANES spectra for two selected Ga-defect-assisted $N-N$ complexes reveal a pronounced sensitivity of the near-edge $\pi^*$ resonance to the local defect environment, providing an atomistic perspective on the experimentally observed evolution toward molecular $N_{2}$ during annealing. Projected densities of states and spin-density distributions show localized N-$2p$- and O-$2p$-derived states well inside the band gap. These vacancy-assisted N complexes therefore provide an atomistic mechanism for deep carrier trapping and current blocking rather than shallow acceptor doping in $\beta-Ga_2O_3$.

item.title: Dynamic Magnetic Pair-Density Function of a One-Dimensional Ferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2608.21759v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamic magnetic pair-density function (DymPDF) $D_{\rm M}(r, E)$ is derived by extending the static magnetic pair distribution function (mPDF) to finite energy transfer. The analytical DymPDF of a one-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet is obtained from the magnon dispersion and compared with simulations performed using {\textsc SpinW}. Excellent agreement is achieved for energy dependence of the nearest-neighbor spin-pair correlation, demonstrating that the DymPDF changes sign at the magnon-mode transition occurring at one-half of the maximum magnon energy. The r-dependence of DymPDF at low energy is also reproduced with a model including magnon correlation length and Fourier-termination effects. These results establish the theoretical foundation of DymPDF analysis for investigating local spin dynamics in magnetic materials.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichi Shamoto

item.title: High-fidelity k$\cdot$p representations of first-principles electronic band structures through covariant renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2609.11861v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The k$\cdot$p method can be applied directly to first-principles energies and momentum matrix elements, but the resulting models converge slowly with the number of bands and are inexact wherever the underlying Hamiltonian is nonlocal. We show that both limitations can be largely removed by renormalizing the eigenvalue spectra of the Hermitian momentum matrices. These spectra are gauge invariant, and are identical along symmetry-related directions; hence scaling the recurring magnitudes provides a modest set of parameters that preserves degeneracies and crystal symmetry without needing to construct a symmetry-adapted basis. We choose to renormalize the models against reference eigenvalues and band velocities on rays out of a high-symmetry point. For GaP, a 15-band model can reproduce the band structure in the near-gap reference regions within a few meV. For zincblende and wurtzite AlN, similar accuracy requires 30- or 85-band models, which in the case of zincblende is traced to the strong warping in the [110] direction. The scheme readily generalizes to rocksalt PbTe, which includes spin-orbit coupling, and has $L$-centered valence- and conduction-band extrema. Further, we demonstrate, for GaP, how compact four-band Hamiltonians can be obtained by downfolding within the same renormalization scheme. Moreover, by changing the fitting regime to encompass the entire Brillouin zone, the scheme can be used to generate full-zone models that reproduce the density of states. A practical use of the method is illustrated with a 59-band k$\cdot$p model for GaP, which can be evaluated on meshes far denser than the reference calculation, that in turn can be used both to resolve fine features in the density of states and to compute the hole conductivity at low temperature.
item.dc:creator: Kristian Berland

item.title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization
item.description: arXiv:2609.14906v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem establishes that, in principle, the ground state (GS) charge density contains all GS information of a many-electron system, such that all GS observables can be expressed as functionals of the GS charge density. Conventional Kohn-Sham density functional theory requires iterative solution of the self-consistent-field equations at substantial computational cost, motivating the development of deep learning surrogates for electronic structure calculations and, in turn, accelerating computer-aided materials design. Here, we propose AIDEN, an Atomic-Interaction Density Equivariant Network for solving real-space charge density. AIDEN separates the element-dependent one-center density from environment-induced density redistribution and represents the latter through complementary atom- and edge-centered tensor correlations. A continuous low-rank Gaussian decoder then reconstructs the density at arbitrary spatial coordinates while reusing atomic encodings independently of the evaluation grid. AIDEN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on periodic crystal benchmarks while remaining competitive for molecular systems, and further demonstrates zero-shot transferability across several structurally distinct out-of-distribution case studies. Furthermore, AIDEN provides substantially faster inference than both baseline models and full SCF calculations, enabling efficient charge density reconstruction for large-scale electronic structure calculations.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Zeng, Tong Xie, Taoyuze Lv, Zhicheng Zhong

item.title: Thermally stimulated depolarization in hafnium oxide: experiment and numerical simulation
item.description: arXiv:2609.15036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents an experimental and theoretical study of thermally stimulated depolarization (TSD) in hafnium oxide. Three different models for the probability of trap ionization are considered: the Frenkel effect and two variants of the multiphonon trap ionization mechanism, the multiphonon ionization mechanism of isolated traps at low trap concentrations and phonon-assisted tunneling between neighboring traps at high trap concentrations. The best agreement between the TSD experiment and theory is observed for the multiphonon ionization mechanism of isolated traps. Similar thermal energies of electron and hole traps in HfO2 are obtained ~ 1.3 eV.
item.dc:creator: Yu. N. Novikov, D. E. Temnov, E. A. Volgina, M. S. Lebedev, V. A. Gritsenko

item.title: Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
item.description: arXiv:2609.22845v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. Moreover, cross-sectional cathodoluminescence measurements on samples with high defect density demonstrate a suppressed quartet-state luminescence from the V$_\mathrm{Si}$ up to 500 nm beneath the Ni contact. This drastic influence on the defect's magnetic environment is accompanied by the appearance of a signature consistent with photoluminescence from the spin-doublet state of V$_\mathrm{Si}$ under the Ni layer, which was absent in other material stacks. These results establish that standard device configurations can drive quantum defects into unwanted charge and spin configurations, underscoring the necessity of precise design to preserve quantum-grade spin environments in semiconductor devices.
